items.quote: To call the API as a user in your workspace, use an OAuth app.
items.why: Supports only the OAuth part of the auth-method list; api_key and bearer_token unaddressed.

items.quote: Each API key carries its own fine-grained permissions.
items.why: Supports per-key fine-grained permissions detail only; not the auth method list.

items.quote: This means that there are no limitations in what can be done via the API vs the UI.
items.why: Directly states no API limitations versus the UI, the claim's key point.

items.quote: Plain itself is built on this same GraphQL API.
items.why: Supports UI built on the API; does not establish the no-limitations or endpoint details.

items.quote: Once connected, your AI client can do almost anything you can do in Plain, across nearly 400 tools.
items.why: Implies a working AI-client MCP server, but not vendor-official status or the URL.

items.quote: You authenticate with your existing Plain account, so the MCP server has the same permissions as your user.
items.why: Describes MCP auth and permissions; does not establish existence, vendor-official status, or URL.
